Theme

Money, work & business · Town, shops & places

guarantee noun

a written promise to repair or replace goods

also warranty, under guarantee, still under guarantee, money-back guarantee, guaranteed

classical

Cic. Fam. 7.18.1: Graeculam tibi mīsī cautiōnem chīrographī meī

1Lewis & Short gives cautiō as “an obligation, security, bond, warranty, bail”; its use for a maker’s or seller’s guarantee on goods is ours.

cautiō1, cautiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a written guarantee, a bond

In law a security or bond, written or spoken, by which one secures another against loss (Lewis & Short). Its everyday sense is care, caution: cautiō est, one must be careful (Plaut., Ter.).

Other words

  • praestātiō, praestātiōnis f. — a warranty, a guaranty

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Sen. Brev. Vit. 13.9: ut ad praestātiōnem scrībant (Lewis & Short); Dig. 45.1.2 (Lewis & Short)

    Post-Augustan, and a jurists’ word (Lewis & Short): the being answerable for something (see guarantee, praestāre).

Examples

  • quoniam vestrae cautiōnēs īnfirmae sunt, Graeculam tibi mīsī cautiōnem chīrographī meī

    since you lawyers’ guarantees are worth so little, I have sent you a little Greek guarantee in my own handCic. Fam. 7.18.1

See also guarantee, contract, receipt, refund.

SourcesLewis & Short: cautio · Lewis & Short: praestatio
